solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Go beserk with back to front threesome!

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is lifted off the back and placed at the front

blocks.note: to run riot is to go berserk

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a group of three running wild and getting everything back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: RIOT with its final T moved to the front becomes TRIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three, especially three musicians playing together.

clue.text: Smart arse member behind Conservative bar

indicators.note: placed behind means this word comes after the other pieces

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
a lever is a bar used to prise or shift things
member is slang for the penis, as is dick

explanation.surface: A rude description of a clever-clogs MP who sits behind a Tory in the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Member and bar look parliamentary; one is ruder than it seems, the other is a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever dick is a show-off who flaunts their knowledge, which is exactly what a smart arse is in British slang.

clue.text: Sexist vibrating gismo? Yes ... no ... yes

definitions.note: adjective standing for a noun: the clue reads loosely as 'sexist attitude'

indicators.note: something vibrating is shaken about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written for the shuffle
Y is short for yes
N is short for no
Y is short for yes again

explanation.surface: A sex toy, hesitantly described as sexist with a dithering yes, no, yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots make the three short words look like hesitation; each is just its initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Misogyny is hatred of or prejudice against women, the core of a sexist attitude.

clue.text: Blunt's hollow intervening in party backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the party's short name is read right to left
something intervening comes between, so it sits inside the other word

blocks.note: LAB is the short form of the Labour Party
a rut is a hollow groove worn in the ground

explanation.surface: A satirical swipe at someone named Blunt whose hollow words support a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunt's' reads as a person, but the definition is blunt and the 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutal can mean harshly direct, as in brutal honesty, which is what blunt describes.

clue.text: Prison unrest

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for jail
second meaning: a commotion or agitation

explanation.surface: A headline about rioting in a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a jail term or jail itself, and also means a disturbance or fuss.

clue.text: Cliff: "Duty everywhere engulfs one" – pain in the arse!

indicators.note: letters scattered everywhere are out of order and must be rearranged
to engulf is to swallow up, so the scrambled letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: both words taken as written for the shuffle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Cliff Richard quoted proclaiming his ever-present sense of duty, which someone finds tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a pronouncement by the singer Cliff Richard; it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficulty is a problem or nuisance, which is what a pain in the arse means in slang.

clue.text: Dicky gets into Stephen's (so it's said) girly underwear

indicators.note: so it's said means we go by the sound of the possessive, not its spelling
getting into something means going inside it

blocks.note: Stephen Fry is the British comic actor; his possessive sounds like a word for chips
dicky is British slang for poorly or unwell

explanation.surface: Tabloid gossip that a man has got into a celebrity's lacy knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name but means sick, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Frillies is informal for frilly, feminine lingerie.

clue.text: Tensing possibly audible when Brenda in mad pash embrace

definitions.note: Tensing is spelled as heard; the climber is usually written Tenzing

indicators.note: mad means wild and disordered, so the next word's letters are rearranged
to embrace is to hold within one's arms, so these letters wrap around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written for the shuffle
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, and ER is the royal cipher Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The Queen caught in a passionate clinch with a mountaineer, loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: Tenzing Norgay, who climbed Everest with Hillary, was a Sherpa; 'possibly' marks him as an example and 'audible' excuses the phonetic spelling. A pash is a crush.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenzing Norgay belonged to the Sherpa people of Nepal, so he is one instance of a Sherpa.

clue.text: Selling back, er, US women as sex objects

indicators.note: going back means the following little word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the hesitation er, taken as written
tail is American slang for women regarded sexually

explanation.surface: A hesitant remark about marketing that sells women as sex objects in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'er' reads as a speaker hesitating, but it supplies two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail is the business of selling goods to the public, so as a noun modifier it stands for selling.

clue.text: Buddhist-like Blair endlessly returning to secure Brown's end (love-in unlikely)

indicators.note: without its end, the name loses its final letter
returning means coming back, so the shortened name is read backwards
an unlikely arrangement is an improbable one, so the letters are jumbled
to secure something is to hold it fast, so the reversed letters close around the others
'end' keeps only the last letter of 'Brown'

blocks.note: Tony Blair's first name, minus its last letter
the last letter of Brown
taken as written for the shuffle

explanation.surface: A dig at the Blair–Brown feud: Blair, posing as serene, trying to see off Gordon Brown with no love lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair and Brown were the rival Labour leaders; here they only supply TONy and the final N of Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddhism teaches ahimsa, harm to no living thing, so a Buddhist-like stance avoids force.

clue.text: (& 23dn.) Rock theme far out? Loud rubbish!

indicators.note: out here means out of place, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: a riff is a repeated phrase in rock music
taken as written for the shuffle
F is forte, loud in music

explanation.surface: A music critic dismissing a far-out, noisy rock tune as garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Riff-raff means disreputable or worthless people, the human rubbish of a place.

clue.text: (& 13ac.) Do toil madly to appear in tabloid images – a favourite activity at Westminster

indicators.note: done madly, the letters are thrown into a crazy order
appearing in something means showing up inside it

blocks.note: a do is a party
taken as written for the shuffle
pics is tabloid-speak for photographs

explanation.surface: Someone works frantically to get into tabloid photos, a classic MP's pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster is the seat of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Party politics, scoring points for one's own side, is what MPs at Westminster are famously fond of.

clue.text: Being a luvvy, quiet shag with Bill – ding-a-ling!

blocks.note: p is piano, quiet in music
a lay is slang for sex, as is shag
AC is short for account, a bill
ting is the sound of a bell

explanation.surface: A theatrical type's discreet fling with a man called Bill, announced with a comic bell.
explanation.walkthrough: A luvvy is British slang for a gushing actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Playacting means acting or pretending in a showy way, which is what a luvvy, an effusive thespian, does.

clue.text: see 12ac.
It could mean the earth in Sun circulation terms, much of Asia?

definitions.text: It could mean the earth in Sun circulation terms

blocks.clueFragment: It could mean the earth in Sun circulation terms
blocks.note: first meaning taken literally: Earth is the third planet out from the Sun
second meaning: the developing nations

explanation.surface: A puzzling note about the earth, the Sun newspaper's sales and Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun circulation' hints at the tabloid's sales, but it means orbiting the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the old term for developing countries, many of them Asian, and literally Earth is the third planet orbiting the Sun.

clue.text: Film star mainly gets screwed without resistance

indicators.note: something screwed is twisted, so its letters are turned into a new order
without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written for the shuffle
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A cynical line that a screen actress mostly gets bedded with no resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' looks like an adverb, but it is the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn Monroe is the archetypal Hollywood screen idol, so her first name stands for a film star.

clue.text: Put on one's back in Strand in no uncertain manner

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a ply is a single strand of yarn or rope
lain, as in having lain down, is to have been on one's back

explanation.surface: Someone sprawled on their back in the Strand, the London street, for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a famous London thoroughfare, but here strand is a thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainly means clearly and unmistakably, leaving no uncertainty.

clue.text: It's sort of lovely, arresting way too zealous a supporter of Blair!

definitions.text: too zealous a supporter of Blair

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant version, so the letters are rearranged
arresting means seizing and holding, so these letters close around the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written for the shuffle
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A wry note that it would be lovely to see an over-keen Blairite arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Levy was Tony Blair's chief fundraiser, arrested in the 2006 cash-for-honours inquiry, so 'arresting' is a topical pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Levy raised money for Blair's Labour Party with such energy that he was questioned by police.

clue.text: Church official against getting changed for male union

indicators.note: changed for means one letter is swapped out and another put in its place

blocks.note: a verger looks after a church and leads processions
v is short for versus, against
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A churchman opposing the change that allows same-sex marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male union' reads as gay marriage; male only gives one letter and union alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A merger is a joining of two things into one, such as two companies combining.

clue.text: Arse extricating Labour's leader from fall from grace

indicators.note: extricating means pulling something out, so a letter is removed
'leader' keeps only the first letter of 'Labour'

blocks.note: to backslide is to relapse into bad ways
the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A rude verdict on a party leader removed after disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Backside is a polite word for the buttocks, which is what arse means.

clue.text: Beds craftily, in a sly movement

indicators.note: movement shifts things about, so the letters go into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written for the shuffle

explanation.surface: A seducer gets people into bed with a sneaky manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' suggests seduction, but it means sets something into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To inlay is to set pieces skilfully into a surface, embedding them with a craftsman's care.

clue.text: Top taken off Dirty Rosy

indicators.note: removing the top means the first letter goes

blocks.note: cruddy is slang for filthy

explanation.surface: Someone strips off in front of a woman called Rosy.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosy looks like a name; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddy describes a healthy reddish complexion, the same as a rosy one.

clue.text: (& 25dn.) TV series made by shits backing white South African movement?

indicators.note: backing up means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: rats are despicable people, as are shits
the Great Trek was the Boer migration into the South African interior

explanation.surface: A sneer at a TV programme produced by unpleasant people supporting white South African politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Trek is the long-running American science-fiction television series.

clue.text: see 11ac.
From which briefs get more than adequate support?

definitions.text: From which briefs get more than adequate support?

blocks.clueFragment: From which briefs get more than adequate support?
blocks.note: surface reading: underpants that offer generous support
setter's reading: briefs are barristers, who are paid handsomely out of litigation

explanation.surface: An advertisement for underwear with extra support.
explanation.walkthrough: A brief is slang for a lawyer, and their generous fees come out of what clients pay.
explanation.definitionFit: The expenses of litigation pay lawyers' fees, famously more than ample support for counsel.

clue.text: see 22ac.
Snide Poles unsettled

blocks.note: S and N are the south and north poles
iffy means doubtful or undecided

explanation.surface: Nasty remarks leave some Polish people uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles looks like a nationality; it is the two magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sniffy means disdainful and contemptuous, close to snide in tone.

clue.text: Spin exponent likely to get fired?

blocks.note: first meaning: one that turns round and round
second meaning: a handgun with a rotating cylinder

explanation.surface: A spin doctor who is probably going to be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Spin and fired suggest a political press officer losing their job.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means something that rotates, and is also a pistol that is discharged by firing.
